Which order of the graphs shows decreasing spring constants?
A
2  1  3  4
B
3  4  2  1
C
4  2  1  3
D
4  3  2  1

hints: Look at the end-point values on each $F$ against $x$ graph: graph 1 is $10\text{ N}$ at $5\text{ mm}$, graph 2 is $20\text{ N}$ at $4\text{ mm}$, graph 3 is $100\text{ N}$ at $0.1\text{ mm}$ and graph 4 is $10\text{ N}$ at $0.5\text{ mm}$.
Recall that for Hooke's law $F = kx$, the spring constant $k$ is the gradient $F/x$ of the $F$ against $x$ line, so a large $F$ with a small $x$ means a stiff spring.
Convert each $x$ from $\text{mm}$ to $\text{m}$ and calculate $k = F/x$ in $\text{N m}^{-1}$ for the four graphs, then list them from largest $k$ to smallest $k$.
walkthrough: Hooke's law is $F = kx$, so the spring constant is the gradient of force against extension: $k = F/x$. The $x$-axes are in $\text{mm}$, so convert to $\text{m}$ using $1\text{ mm} = 1 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}$.
Comparing values: $1.0 \times 10^{6} > 20000 > 5000 > 2000$, so decreasing stiffness is $3 \rightarrow 4 \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 1$.

A.explanation: This order puts graph 2 first, but graph 3 has a much larger $F/x$ ratio and graph 4 is also stiffer than graph 2.

B.explanation: Graph 3 gives the largest $k$ and graph 1 the smallest, with $k_3 > k_4 > k_2 > k_1$ when $k=F/x$ is calculated in consistent units.

C.explanation: This order puts graph 4 before graph 2 correctly but wrongly places graph 3 last, whereas graph 3 has the largest force for the smallest extension.

D.explanation: This order swaps graphs 3 and 4, but $100\text{ N}$ for $0.1\text{ mm}$ in graph 3 gives a larger $k$ than $10\text{ N}$ for $0.5\text{ mm}$ in graph 4.
